newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Israel interested in Russian natgas, no deal yet.
newsitem.headline: Israel interested in Russian natgas, no deal yet.

text.p: Israel is interested in buying natural gas from Russia but has not yet worked out the details of an agreement, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said at the end of an official visit to Moscow on Wednesday.
"I discussed the general idea of Israel's purchasing gas from Russia," Netanyahu told a news conference. "I said 'we're waiting, frankly, for an offer.'"
"If the price is right and the terms of trade are right, we have every interest to diversify our energy supply."

Netanyahu, who met President Boris Yeltsin and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday, said ministry officials from both countries would discuss details of an agreement in "the very near future".
The Israeli press has reported that Netanyahu was interested in purchasing about $3 billion in gas if he could get Russia to agree not to sell weapons to Iran and Syria.

Netanyahu did not give details of any possible deal, but said: "We didn't offer a quid pro quo via gas, but yes, of course, I did raise the question of ballistic missile and nuclear technology flowing to Iran."
The Israeli leader is scheduled to return to Jerusalem later on Wednesday.
